Pertinent

PUR-tuh-nent -- shares a root with 'pertain,' meaning to relate to. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pertinent is relevant or applicable to the particular matter at hand.

Only questions pertinent to the case were allowed during the cross-examination.

Worked Example

A doctor reviewing a patient's chart before surgery skips over the patient's favorite hobbies and focuses only on allergies, past surgeries, and current medications.

That narrow focus on exactly what matters for the task at hand is exactly what pertinent describes. Unlike 'interesting,' which can apply to anything engaging, pertinent specifically means directly relevant to the matter.

How Pertinent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

relevant

relevant: directly related to the matter being discussed

applicable

applicable: able to be applied to a particular situation

germane

germane: relevant to the matter at hand

Antonyms

irrelevant

irrelevant: not related to the matter at hand

extraneous

extraneous: unrelated or unnecessary to the main subject

How Strong Is It? — applicable → pertinent → germane

applicable vs. pertinent

applicable vs. pertinent: Applicable is broader than pertinent -- applicable can describe a rule or fact that generally applies, while pertinent specifically emphasizes direct relevance to the exact matter being discussed.

germane vs. pertinent

germane vs. pertinent: Germane can feel even more precise than pertinent: pertinent means generally relevant, while germane implies an especially close, essential connection to the specific topic.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — per-

Prefix — per-: through, thoroughly (Latin)

Root — tin

Root — tin: to hold (from Latin tenere, 'to hold' — the same root spelled tain in retain)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: adjective-forming (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Per- ('through, thoroughly') + tin ('to hold' — from Latin tenere) + -ent (adjective-forming): Latin pertinere meant 'to extend to' or 'belong to.' Something pertinent, at its root, 'holds through' to the matter — it stays connected and relevant to it.

Use the root in a new word: retain

Use the root in a new word: retain: The company worked hard to retain its best employees by offering better benefits.
